sources.entry: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is a subset of artificial intelligence that uses generative models to produce text, images, videos, or other forms of data.

summary.name: Artificial intelligence (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia overview of artificial intelligence: the field of computational systems performing human-like tasks such as learning, reasoning, perception and decision-making, covering its goals, techniques, history and applications.
use_cases: learning the basics of artificial intelligence
researching the history of AI and AI winters
reviewing AI applications in health and search
getting an overview of machine learning and neural networks
summary.what_it_does: The page is a general encyclopedia article describing artificial intelligence as a field and its traditional goals: reasoning, knowledge representation, planning, natural language processing, perception, and robotics support. It outlines techniques used in AI research, including state space search, local search such as gradient descent, formal logic, probabilistic methods, classifiers, and artificial neural networks. It covers machine learning types (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, transfer, deep learning) and modern large language models and GPTs. It also gives a brief history from the 1956 founding through AI winters to the post-2012 deep learning and 2020s generative AI boom, with examples in health and everyday applications.
notable: Broad reference covering goals, techniques, history and applications of AI
Explains neural networks, deep learning, LLMs and GPT models in plain structure
Describes AI winters and cycles of optimism in the field's history
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software tool; it does not offer downloadable products
Page text is truncated and some sections (such as AI-assisted software development, chatbots, physical AI) have no body text
